item.description: Dolly using her platform for environmental awareness alongside her music career shows how celebrities can meaningfully engage with causes beyond just performing her tennessee roots clearly shaped that genuine connection to nature conservation Tushar Arora Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Cellular 'glue' helps epithelial tissues engulf dead cells while staying sealed
item.description: A protein that sticks cells and tissues together has been found to have a surprising second job: helping cells that are packed into a continuous sealed layer, also known as epithelial cells, engulf nearby dead cells. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fleeting sugar pairs may help curb abnormal cell-growth signals
item.description: Acting as armor, a scaffold and a communication platform in one, our cells' plasma membrane lies at the heart of many crucial cellular processes. Traditionally, it has been thought to function through interactions among its various proteins and lipids. Now, researchers have revealed a crucial yet often overlooked membrane component—complex sugar chains, known as glycans, carried by certain membrane lipids called gangliosides and many membrane proteins. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scented cleaners can create nanoparticles that reach deep into the lungs within minutes, tiny-home experiment finds
item.description: What does a clean room smell like? Many people say citrus, pine, or flowers because these fragrances are common in cleaning products. A research team led by Brandon Boor found that scent compounds in cleaning products—conventional and botanical essential oil-based—quickly react in the air, forming nanoparticles that can travel deep into the lungs if inhaled. To reduce exposure to this invisible pollution, the team suggests using unscented products, running exhaust fans, and avoiding ozone-generating devices while cleaning. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Light particles reveal critical scaling in a two-dimensional photon gas
item.description: A team of researchers from the University of Bonn, Heidelberg University and the National Autonomous University of Mexico has studied the critical behavior of light particles (photons) close to a phase transition. This critical scaling behavior, which sees thermodynamic quantities grow extremely large or diverge shortly prior to Bose-Einstein condensation, had never before been seen in photon gases until the researchers successfully secured precisely this proof. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How to keep your child's tablets, laptops from becoming distractions from schoolwork
item.description: Tablets and computers have become crucial school supplies for many students. But the same devices children use to read text, write essays, solve math problems or research history projects can also offer distractions in the form of games, social media and web browsing. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Virtual cell model could accelerate protein-degrader therapy design
item.description: A team of Weill Cornell Medicine investigators has developed a computer model that will help scientists more efficiently develop protein-destroying therapies, a newer type of treatment that is particularly promising for cancer. The study is published July 13 in Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Expedition Sound podcast series
item.description: Expedition Sound is a podcast series by the European Space Agency (ESA) in which you’re invited to explore the Universe through your ears. Guided by sonifications – the translation of data into sound – host Zsófi Szalavári travels from our Sun out into the depths of space to uncover what the space telescopes of ESA’s science missions teach us about the Universe. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: MTG-I2 ready for launch on Ariane 6
item.description: The Meteosat Third Generation Imager2 satellite (MTG-I2) has been encapsulated inside the Ariane 6 fairing and is in place on its launch pad. It is scheduled to lift off on Thursday evening, 27 August, from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 August 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Colorful Aurora over […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Some Galápagos 'yellow' sea turtles remain homebodies, surprising scientists
item.description: Sea turtles are famous for being prodigious wanderers. Guided by Earth's magnetic field, ocean currents and the sun, they tend to crisscross the seas in search of food, returning to the region of their birth every few years to breed. So when scientists discovered a population of sea turtles that appear to be very much homebodies, they were taken aback. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: We finally have some encouraging news on Great Barrier Reef water quality
item.description: Imagine a plume of brown sediment washed off the land into Queensland rivers and carried out to sea. Here, it can settle on seagrass and inshore corals, potentially smothering them. River water often also carries nitrogen from fertilizer residue, which can fuel algal growth and damage coral health. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Team identifies an evolutionarily conserved enhancer that regulates tendon and ligament development
item.description: A research team has uncovered fundamental molecular mechanisms governing the formation of tendons and ligaments, which are essential for musculoskeletal integration. Understanding these mechanisms could pave the way for the regeneration of tendons, ligaments and their attachment sites, known as entheses, which have limited capacity for functional repair after injury because of their poor vascularization. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The crisis in cosmology continues: Critical problems in a recent defense of cosmic acceleration
item.description: Doubts about the standard model of cosmology are deepening after a new study identified fundamental problems in a recent analysis that defended the conventional view that the universe is currently undergoing accelerated expansion driven by dark energy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Virtual reality reveals glassfish synchronize through split-second copying of single neighbors
item.description: For centuries, scientists have been fascinated by the remarkable coordinated movements of flocking birds, swarming insects and schooling fish. Researchers have studied these natural phenomena to understand the rules of interactions between individuals that can produce complex group-level behavior. A collaboration of physicists and neurobiologists at the University of California San Diego has been studying schools of micro glassfish (Danionella cerebrum) to understand how the interactive mental processes of individual fish produce group-level decisions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chris Michael Hughes ha comentado: How can you have an eclipse at night? It's already dark
item.description: A partial lunar eclipse will pass over the Americas—and parts of Europe and Africa—tomorrow night! It will reach its peak around 12:12 a.m. EDT (0412... Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Reworked tRNAs enable protein design with up to 34 amino acids
item.description: Scientists have been hard at work for more than 20 years to instruct biological systems, such as E. coli cells, to produce proteins they don't naturally produce. Success could mean faster, cheaper, more innovative solutions for medicine, agriculture, materials science, environmental remediation and other industries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Innovative etching method for silicon: Higher precision through interlayer
item.description: In micro- and nanotechnology, highly precise components with tall, narrow structures (high aspect ratios) made from semiconductor materials like silicon are important. A promising fabrication method is gas-phase metal-assisted chemical etching (MacEtch). In this plasma-free process, a thin metal layer defines the pattern on the silicon substrate. The etching step takes place in a chemical environment, where the reaction occurs only at the interface between the metal and silicon. The metal catalyst gradually sinks into the silicon, directing the etching deeper. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI framework challenges student ideas early, helping undergraduates think critically about research
item.description: An interdisciplinary team of researchers has developed and demonstrated a step-by-step framework called Socratic Challenger that uses artificial intelligence to help undergraduate students cultivate critical thinking skills. Specifically, the framework uses AI as a collaborator to develop research questions that can be pursued in laboratory or classroom settings. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How plants use scoop-shaped pores to distribute their pollen efficiently
item.description: Bees are the most important pollinators of flowering plants, and approximately 10% of flowering plants are functionally specialized for buzz pollination. Buzz pollination is a mechanism in which pollen can be extracted from flowers only through the application of mechanical vibrations. Many important crops, such as tomatoes, eggplants and blueberries, are buzz-pollinated because they conceal their pollen in so-called poricidal anthers—floral structures with only a minute opening through which pollen can be released only when mechanical vibrations are applied. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Electrically charged raindrops could be corroding metal with protective coatings
item.description: Electrically charged raindrops, a naturally occurring phenomenon, can break down surfaces treated with protective coatings, according to new research published in Nature. This previously overlooked corrosion mechanism highlights the need for a new method of preserving metal objects like cars, ships, buildings and cultural heritage sites. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The 'Rock of Starvation' reappears as drought tightens its grip on the Danube
item.description: The reappearance of Budapest's "Rock of Starvation" is a visible sign of a drought months in the making. IIASA researchers have traced its progression from missing rainfall and parched soils to exceptionally low flows across the Danube basin. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ramped fields create more robust entanglement between trapped-ion qubits
item.description: While quantum computing could be the future, it is currently plagued by finicky hardware. To make the technology practical, researchers must demonstrate that it consistently and continuously works and performs at scale. In a new study, published in Physical Review Letters, researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) and the Ion Storage Group at the National Institute of Standards and Technology in Boulder, Colorado, created a robust process for entangling trapped-ion qubits. The result means better building blocks for ion-based quantum computers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: We discovered rare dinosaur tracks from the Coniacian age near Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia
item.description: Imagine the Western Plains of North America, from Texas to Alaska, submerged under a broad, shallow seaway. To the west lay the ancestral Rocky Mountains. To the east were low-lying plains traversed by large, sluggish rivers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: European city climate plans underuse green spaces despite adaptation benefits, finds study
item.description: Green spaces could play a key role in helping cities cope with the effects of climate change, yet they still play only a minor role in climate strategies. These were the findings of researchers at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (MLU) and Justus Liebig University Giessen (JLU), who analyzed the climate strategies of 25 major European cities. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: US seizes Chinese hacking platforms targeting Nasa, Fed and Senate
item.description: The Justice Department and the FBI said on Wednesday that they seized two Chinese state-sponsored online platforms that targeted US critical infrastructure and other critical networks, including Nasa, the Federal Reserve and the US Senate. According to court documents, the seizures involved a group known as “QTFY”, operated by China-based Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Co, which created and ran the QScan and QTRouter sites. “State-sponsored malicious hackers preying on America’s critical... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Mark Magnier

item.title: Reference genome of the Saimaa ringed seal released
item.description: Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland and the University of Oulu have produced the first chromosome-level reference genome for the Saimaa ringed seal. The sequence of every chromosome in the seal's entire genome has now been read and assembled into virtual maps, including its gene content. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Does AI shape decisions before we do? Researcher questions what 'human in the loop' really means
item.description: Artificial intelligence is often discussed with a simple safeguard in mind: Keep a human in the loop. But what happens when AI is already shaping the information, options and recommendations that inform a decision? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How plants evolved a molecular switch to cope with heat
item.description: As climate change drives more frequent and intense heat waves, plants face growing challenges to survive and remain productive. Researchers at VIB, Ghent University, KU Leuven and their international collaborators have uncovered an evolutionary innovation that helps plants cope with high temperatures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hidden switch in cell division may point to new cancer treatments
item.description: When a cell gets ready to divide, it shuts down its gene-reading machinery almost entirely. For decades, the mechanism behind that shutdown was only partially understood. A new study co-led by Alarcón and Lilian Kabeche, associate professor of molecular biophysics and biochemistry at Yale School of Medicine, identifies a missing piece: an enzyme best known for tagging RNA molecules that turns out to be wired into the cell division machinery itself. The findings, recently published in Molecular Cell, may point toward new cancer therapies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Political divide traced to differing views on who is vulnerable
item.description: Everyone shares a similar moral compass about right and wrong, but where liberals and conservatives disagree is over who counts as a victim, according to new research from the University at Buffalo School of Management. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Australia's lizards and snakes disappearing faster than previously thought
item.description: Australia's lizards and snakes are facing a far more precarious future than previously understood, with a new review led by Monash University researchers revealing that around 127 species, or just over 13% of Australia's terrestrial lizards and snakes, are now likely to be threatened with extinction—almost double previous estimates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Unexpected source of genetic diversity found in human sperm
item.description: Scientists have identified an unexpected source of genetic variation in human sperm that occurs earlier in sperm development than previously thought. Published in Nature, researchers at the Wellcome Sanger Institute, the University of Cambridge and their collaborators found that one type of genetic recombination involving chromosomes, called non-crossover gene conversion, happens before the cell divisions that produce sperm. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Machine learning methods move self-driving labs closer to materials discovery at scale
item.description: Machine learning doesn't replace human intelligence, but it can outlast human endurance, which makes it a helpful tool for chemistry and materials discovery. Scientists know machine learning models can make predictions based on the vast reams of data they are trained on, but can they take it a step further and massively scale up testing those predictions? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Basalt weathering may remove far less CO₂ than projected
item.description: Spreading finely crushed basalt across farmland has been promoted as a relatively simple way to remove large quantities of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. But a new study led by Cornell researchers suggests the real-world potential of this method, known as enhanced weathering, may be far smaller than widely cited estimates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Thermal anomaly discovered below Mars' south pole
item.description: Researchers have discovered a thermal asymmetry deep beneath the surface across Mars' southern hemisphere. Based on gravitational measurements that provide clues to the Red Planet's interior structure, Mars' southern interior is around 200 to 400 degrees Celsius warmer than the planet's northern half and partially molten. The surprising finding adds context to Martian history and the periods during which it may have hosted conditions favorable for life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Disappearing lakes, old photos and AI are helping scientists map Arctic permafrost thaw in near‑real time
item.description: Florida gets a lot of attention for its sinkholes, especially when they swallow cars and entire houses. But its sinkhole risk has nothing on Alaska's. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI designs new antibodies that pass blinded laboratory tests
item.description: Researchers affiliated with UTHealth Houston, competing under the team name Novamab AI, placed among the top five teams in the international AIntibody Challenge, a blinded, prospective benchmark published in Nature Biotechnology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sunscreen for lakes and dams: Could a thin floating layer of nanomaterial shield water from evaporation?
item.description: Water stored in dams and reservoirs for humans to use often evaporates, especially in hot regions like southern Africa. Rising temperatures speed up evaporation, leaving less water for people, farming and industry. Daniel Kwasi Kpeglo has just completed a Ph.D. in physics. He explains his laboratory research into a new design—a thin nanomaterial floating cover that could be placed over lakes and dams like a blanket, reducing evaporation by limiting the amount of infrared heat from the sun that reaches the water. He also outlines what hurdles need to be cleared for the design to be tested in… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Permafrost thaws worldwide as active layers deepen from 2000 to 2024
item.description: An international study led by researchers at the George Washington University indicates clear global evidence that permafrost is thawing across much of the planet. Using more than two decades of field observations from 156 monitoring sites across the Arctic, Antarctic and high-mountain regions, the study found increases in the thickness of the active layer, the uppermost layer above permafrost that thaws and refreezes each year. The findings confirm that permafrost degradation accelerated globally between 2000 and 2024. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why banks in Ghana make little use of AI for climate action decisions
item.description: Artificial intelligence could help evaluate climate protection projects more effectively and channel funding more precisely to where it is needed. Nevertheless, banks and insurance companies in Ghana have so far made very little use of the technology. A new study conducted at the Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus-Senftenberg (BTU) in collaboration with the Durban University of Technology in South Africa investigated the reasons behind this. The study is published in Discover Sustainability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Europa se prepara para llegar a Marte usando energía nuclear
item.description: La Agencia Espacial Europea analiza cómo usar esta herramienta en lugar de los combustibles químicos que se usan actualmente. Países como Francia, Bélgica y República Checa avanzan en el desarrollo de tecnologías novedosas. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.
item.dc:creator: Clarin.com - Home

item.title: Dry seeds preserve fully formed mitochondria, unlocking rapid energy at germination
item.description: The majority of plant seeds have the special ability to almost completely dry out and yet remain viable. While most living cells die with a 90% loss of water, cells in seeds enter a biological state of dormancy. With a moisture content of less than 10%—similar to a raisin compared to a grape—they become small time capsules and can lie dormant for decades until they are awakened by favorable environmental conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Yale researchers find a new way to make PFAS easier to remove and destroy
item.description: Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Fossil-fuel carbon fingerprint reaches the deep North Atlantic
item.description: The use of fossil fuels alters both the concentration and the carbon isotope composition of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. Since surface water exchanges carbon dioxide with the atmosphere, this also alters the isotopic composition of the carbon dissolved in the ocean. In a new study, a team from MARUM—Center for Marine Environmental Sciences at the University of Bremen has now determined how deep this so-called Suess effect has already penetrated into the North Atlantic. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Building Foresight for Earth Science, featuring Lindsey Jacobson
item.description: NASA’s Earth-observing satellite missions track dozens of features of a changing planet — aerosols, sea levels, land cover, cloud cover — over years and decades. Sustaining that record for the scientific and operational communities who depend on it requires more than engineering talent. It requires planning for an uncertain future: anticipating where a mission delay […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Sondra Woodward

item.title: For Legionella bacteria, taking over a cell means playing by its rules
item.description: When it comes to invading healthy cells, Legionella bacteria rely on blending in rather than breaking in. New research from Van Andel Institute scientists demonstrates how a protein produced by Legionella mimics the behavior of the host cell's own proteins. This mechanism allows the protein, RomA, to change how the host's genes are regulated and create conditions that help the bacteria survive and multiply. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Older women experience sexual violence too, but their stories rarely make the news
item.description: The reality of sexual violence against older women is an issue that remains significantly underreported and misrepresented in Australia. Almost 50 sexual assaults occur every week in aged care. Sexual assault against older women is commonly perpetrated by intimate partners or someone they know. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Roman telescope aims to directly image exoplanets 1,000 times fainter than current limits
item.description: The Roman Space Telescope is designed to directly image exoplanets using complex optomechanical systems developed by the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Roman Space Telescope Travels to SpaceX Hangar
item.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, encapsulated in its payload fairing, travels from the Payload Hazardous Servicing Facility to the SpaceX hangar at Launch Complex 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, ahead of mating to a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. Roman’s science instruments are designed to help researchers understand dark […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Liquid gallium experiment confirms key flow regime inside rapidly rotating stars and planets
item.description: Since we cannot look into the interiors of stars and planets, we rely on lab experiments to replicate the physical processes that occur there. Led by the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), an international research team has produced the first experimental verification of a theoretically predicted flow state deemed characteristic of the interiors of rapidly rotating celestial bodies. The Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) also participated in the study, which has been published in Physical Review Letters. The results provide a robust experimental basis for testing… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Genetic traces reveal river residents: 1,072 species in a bucket of water
item.description: Can DNA traces in just two liters (0.5 gallons) of water reveal how a river's biodiversity changes over the course of a year? A study by the University of Duisburg-Essen using the River Lippe as an example shows how biodiversity in freshwater ecosystems can be monitored comprehensively, efficiently and at comparatively low cost. The results have now been published in the journal Ecological Indicators. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Better timetables could greatly shorten train travel times
item.description: Anyone traveling by train across Europe spends a surprisingly large portion of the trip not on a moving train. Today, about 25% of travel time is spent on transfers and layovers at train stations because of poorly coordinated timetables. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When fruits and veggies are scarce, monkeys hunt for meat
item.description: Capuchin monkeys hunt prey when fruits and vegetables become scarce, potentially mirroring the habits of human ancestors, according to a study published in PLOS One by Susana Carvalho (Gorongosa National Park, Mozambique), Noemi Spagnoletti (Sapienza University of Rome, Italy) and colleagues. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Many workplaces resist plant-based lunches despite substantial climate benefits
item.description: Are organizations ready for plant-based food at work? A new study from the University of Copenhagen explores this question and shows that only a small proportion of workplaces in Denmark are ready for this change—despite its potential to reduce the climate footprint of workplace lunches. In general, introducing plant-based food is likely to stir strong emotions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tiny atomic changes could lead to smarter wireless technology
item.description: Researchers at Queen Mary University of London have shown that making extremely small changes to the structure of a material can dramatically improve its ability to respond to electrical signals. Published recently in Science Advances, the breakthrough could help create a new generation of wireless devices that can change frequency on demand, making communication systems more flexible and energy efficient. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Narwhals help researchers uncover unique data from the deepest East Greenland fjords
item.description: They live in some of the most inaccessible waters on Earth, where ocean temperatures hover around freezing. Because they move through areas that humans rarely reach, they have been able to help researchers with a special task. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chagas parasite's survival trick offers antimalarial-style target
item.description: Researchers at the University of Cincinnati have identified a potential new target to prevent the spread of Chagas disease. The parasitic infection is transmitted through the bite of the kissing bug in Central and South America and, more recently, in the United States. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Johnson Pilots Chase Moon’s Shadow for Eclipse Science
item.description: During the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse over Europe, scientists aimed to study a long-standing mystery: why the Sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona, is far hotter than its visible surface. Capturing the data they needed meant being in exactly the right place at exactly the right time. Pilots from NASA’s Johnson Space Center flew the WB-57F high altitude research aircraft from Ellington Field in Houston to Iceland, […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Sumer Loggins

item.title: Did ocean motion carve Enceladus's tiger stripes?
item.description: Saturn's moon Enceladus sports a thick shell of ice surrounding a liquid water ocean. As though scraped by an enormous claw, four parallel cracks slash across its south pole. Each about 500 meters (1,600 feet) deep, 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) across and 130 kilometers (81 miles) long, the fissures spew water vapor and other materials from the subsurface ocean directly into space. But the origin of these "tiger stripes" is mysterious. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Even protected Florida wetlands can't escape microplastic pollution
item.description: Microplastics are turning up almost everywhere—from oceans and rivers to soils and sediments—yet far less is known about what happens when they enter freshwater wetlands. Often overlooked in favor of marine and coastal environments, wetlands can act as both pathways and traps for microplastics, potentially capturing and retaining pollution. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: G-me Jay ha comentado: So the photographer climbed and reached before them?
item.description: Photographer Cory Richards captured climbers near the summit of Gasherbrum II in Pakistan’s Karakoram Range in 2011. During the descent, the climbers,... Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: How high scores in an online brain teaser made mathematicians lie for three years
item.description: It might not yet be the phenomenon that is Wordle, but for hundreds of thousands of players, Digit Party has scratched the itch of a casual brain teaser to break up their day. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Expert Comment: More extreme weather is coming—AI may help us to better prepare for it
item.description: As of August 2026, the world is bracing for what forecasters describe as one of the strongest El Niño events on record. The U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center has put the chance of a very strong event this fall and winter above 90%, with a 69% likelihood that it will exceed every El Niño since 1950. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reconstructed Jurassic insect calls evoke a 165-million-year-old forest soundscape
item.description: The sights and sounds of the Jurassic era are long gone, and we will never know for sure what that ancient world looked and sounded like. Fossils can offer clues, and reconstructions can give us a sense of the noises some animals might have made. Now scientists have turned their attention to insects and reconstructed the calls of Jurassic relatives of modern-day crickets and katydids (grasshopper-like insects). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Looking into the eyes of gibbons: New noninvasive eye-tracking study features these little-studied apes
item.description: When you look at someone, you usually look at their face. It serves as one of the most important sources of social information in primates, so the evolution of face perception has attracted considerable scientific attention. While an abundance of this research has centered on humans and other great apes, very little has focused on gibbons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fed, NASA and DOJ among victims of Chinese state-sponsored hacker group, FBI says
item.description: An affidavit named the U.S. Department of Energy, HHS, NIH, and four unnamed companies in the United States and South Korea as victims compromised by the hackers Publicado también por: CNBC - World. Fuente: The Independent - World.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter and AJ Vicens

item.title: Human activity is pushing lakes beyond their natural carbon limits
item.description: Lakes play an important role in capturing and storing carbon, which accumulates in their sediments. But the amounts they can absorb have varied considerably over time. Jean-François Lapierre, a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at Université de Montréal, is part of a research team sorting out natural variations from human-influenced changes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers develop hydrogels to create a programmable niche for blood stem cells
item.description: A research team from Tel Aviv University and the Leibniz Institute of Polymer Research Dresden (IPF), led by Ayala Lampel and Carsten Werner, has developed a peptide-glycosaminoglycan hydrogel system that creates a programmable niche for hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). The system mimics key biochemical and mechanical cues of the bone marrow microenvironment, enabling researchers to investigate how these signals influence stem cell behavior. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: G-me Jay ha comentado: So the photographer climbed and reached before them?
item.description: Photographer Cory Richards captured climbers near the summit of Gasherbrum II in Pakistan’s Karakoram Range in 2011. During the descent, the climbers,... Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Narrow ultrasonic beam enables stable 3D levitation six times farther than before
item.description: Scientists have developed a new acoustic levitation technique using an ultrasonic beam capable of levitating and moving small objects in midair over distances of up to 40 cm (16 inches), six times farther than previously achieved using conventional methods. The study, carried out by a research team from the University of Tsukuba in Japan and the University of Bristol, was published in the journal Physical Review Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: CanopyFit maps urban tree sites with greatest cooling potential
item.description: UBC researchers and municipal partners have developed a modeling tool to help cities adapt to rising temperatures by mapping where new trees offer the greatest cooling impact. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fed, NASA and DOJ among victims of China hacker group: Court documents
item.description: Hackers targeted networks "operated by hospitals, telecommunications providers, power companies, financial institutions, and defense contractors," a filing said. Publicado también por: The Independent - World. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Tax break 'megadeals' spurred innovation in local communities
item.description: When cities, counties or states provide corporations with big tax breaks to lure factories, corporate headquarters and other facilities, the economic benefits may go beyond the new jobs and investments the companies bring to their regions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why some lava-covered exoplanets retain atmospheres for billions of years
item.description: Stanford researchers have offered an explanation for why some sizzling, lava-covered worlds nestled tightly around their stars can retain their atmospheres. At such close quarters, intense stellar radiation should strip away a planet's air. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Some music 'Hits Different': Harvard study shows link between music and fatal car accidents in US
item.description: The researchers examined 10 prominent albums released in the United States between 2017 and 2022, including Taylor Swift's Midnights, Harry Styles's Harry's House, and Drake's Certified Lover Boy. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.
item.dc:creator: BY UDI ETZION

item.title: SpaceX is 'attractively valued' after $100 billion Louisiana spaceport plan, Morgan Stanley says
item.description: Investors aren't appreciating the full scope of the rocket maker's plan to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Tangled plastic and fishing gear found in pilot whales stranded in Hawaii
item.description: A new study by University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa researchers shows that nearly 23% of short-finned pilot whales that stranded over 13 years in the main Hawaiian Islands ingested several pounds of plastic ropes, netting, fishing gear and plastic bags discarded in the ocean. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: No sick days? How remote work is changing the way we work when ill
item.description: Working from home and digital technology may be making it easier for employees to work while ill and blurring the boundaries between work and home, according to a new study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers get two genetic codes to work at the same time
item.description: Messing with the genetic code might have gotten a bit easier to do. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: John Timmer

item.title: Nanoparticles induce neuroregeneration in Alzheimer's disease models
item.description: The adult human brain has limited capacity to repair or regenerate neurons lost to Alzheimer's disease, the most common type of dementia. Existing treatments can slow disease progression but do not reverse cognitive decline. In a study published in the journal Cell Biomaterials on Aug. 26, researchers show that engineered nanoparticles can not only regenerate neurons in human brain organoids but also restore neural circuits and improve cognition in mice. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One molecule, one photon: Entanglement makes an imperceptible recoil measurable
item.description: For decades, light has been used to understand the molecular structures of matter. A sample is irradiated with light, and measurements determine the wavelengths at which it is absorbed. Since each molecule absorbs light at very specific wavelengths that depend on its structure, the resulting absorption spectrum acts like a molecular fingerprint. For individual molecules, however, this signal is vanishingly small and mostly indistinguishable from noise. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sharpening an essential tool for biotechnology
item.description: Scientists at the Department of Energy (DOE)'s Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) have shown that more than 93% of possible E. coli CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNAs—molecules that direct the gene-editing CRISPR tool to the right spot in DNA—work as intended, a far higher percentage than researchers expected. They also discovered why a small number of guides fail and developed a simple way to repair them. The work is published in the journal Nucleic Acids Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI robot trains teachers to handle heated issues
item.description: Researchers at La Trobe University are using a robot driven by artificial intelligence (AI) to better prepare teachers to deal with challenging conversations in schools. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: High magnetic fields revive superconductivity in nickelates
item.description: Scientists from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with Los Alamos National Laboratory in the United States, have uncovered that a class of nickel-based materials known as samarium (Sm)-based infinite-layer nickelates can regain their superconducting ability under strong magnetic fields. This behavior could open a promising pathway toward superconducting technologies that can operate under extreme magnetic conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Comet 220P McNaught puts on an encore performance
item.description: It has been a busy month for astronomy. In the midst of an eclipse season bookended by the total solar eclipse on Aug. 12 and the deep partial lunar eclipse coming up this week on Aug. 28, an outbound comet hanging high in the dawn sky just refuses to die: 220P/McNaught. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: LLM-based platform for generating new materials synthesis recipes dramatically cuts trial and error
item.description: A research team led by Professor Sung Beom Cho of the School of Advanced Materials Science and Engineering at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), in collaboration with the teams of Professors Jin Sung Park and Hyunsouk Cho of Ajou University and Professor Ju Li of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), has developed a "closed-loop materials synthesis planning platform" that uses a large language model (LLM) to propose synthesis conditions and procedures for complex new materials and iteratively refine them based on experimental results. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Sets Spacewalk for Station Maintenance, Live Coverage Planned
item.description: NASA will provide coverage as two astronauts step outside the International Space Station on Tuesday, Sept. 1, to replace a spacecraft navigational aid and complete several maintenance tasks in support of space station operations. Watch live coverage beginning at 7 a.m. EDT. The spacewalk is expected to start at approximately 8:30 a.m. and last about […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer M. Dooren

item.title: This image looks peaceful but the story behind it is intense. Surviving a grade 4 avalanche on Gasherbrum II and then talking openly about the trauma takes real courage. Respect…
item.description: This image looks peaceful but the story behind it is intense. Surviving a grade 4 avalanche on Gasherbrum II and then talking openly about the trauma takes real courage. Respect to Cory Richards for turning that experience into a conversation about mental health. Shakil Ahmed Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Too hot to incubate: Nile crocodiles hatch on their own in French reserve
item.description: France's heat waves have produced an unusual outcome at a wildlife park, where 10 Nile crocodiles hatched without human assistance for the first time, the director of the reserve said Wednesday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Parents are increasingly abusive toward teachers and principals. How can schools respond?
item.description: Some private schools have begun asking parents to sign a code of conduct to try to stop abusive behavior toward teachers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A field guide for the Wild West of AI-assisted environmental science
item.description: Researchers at UC Santa Barbara's National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis (NCEAS) are blazing a trail through the Wild West of AI-assisted science, with a field guide aimed at environmental data scientists. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Begins Moon Mission Plume-Surface Interaction Tests
item.description: EDITOR’S NOTE: This story, originally published in December, was revised Aug. 26, 2026 with an update on a new phase of testing, including video from a recent test run and new images. To help NASA and commercial partners better understand the science of lunar landings, specifically the hazards that may occur when a lander’s engine […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Atkinson

item.title: Dogs may use blinking as a subtle social signal
item.description: Blinking keeps eyes moist, sweeps away bits of dirt and dust, and helps the brain rest when processing visual information. But in dogs, it may also serve another function as a subtle social signal. That was one of the conclusions of new research published in the journal Royal Society Open Science, which found that dogs blink more often when they see their owners blinking. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Jeret Howard
item.description: At 17, Jeret Howard raised his right hand to serve his country as a United States Army combat medic in Iraq. This past summer, he raised his right hand again at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Hired as a civil servant under the agency’s workforce directive to restore core competencies by […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: LaToya Dean

item.title: David Rosario ha comentado: National Geographic images like this remind us that behind every "perfect" shot is real risk and real people.
item.description: Photographer Cory Richards captured climbers near the summit of Gasherbrum II in Pakistan’s Karakoram Range in 2011. During the descent, the climbers,... Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: 14 fossilised teeth from Egypt reveal five extinct ancient shark species
item.description: Fossilised shark teeth from Egypt's Western Desert reveal prehistoric ocean life. Scientists discovered teeth from five extinct shark species in the Abu-Tartur Plateau region. These ancient predators inhabited warm tropical seas during the Late Cretaceous period. The findings expand the known record of shark diversity in North Africa. This discovery highlights Egypt's ancient marine environments hidden beneath its deserts. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Creíamos que bolsas y pajitas eran el culpable de la contaminación oceánica. Pero lo que llena el gran vertedero del Pacífico es muy diferente
item.description: La imagen popular de la contaminación oceánica lleva décadas construida alrededor de bolsas de supermercado, botellas, vasos de plástico y pajitas que abandonamos en tierra y terminan llegando al mar. A escala global esa imagen tiene bastante de cierto: los ríos y las zonas costeras siguen siendo grandes vías de entrada de plástico al océano. El problema es que cuando los investigadores fueron a buscar esos residuos a una de las mayores acumulaciones de basura marina del planeta encontraron una fotografía muy distinta. La trampa oceánica. La Gran Mancha de Basura del Pacífico no es la… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Jorge

item.title: Scientists may have found a shortcut to calorie restriction’s anti-aging benefits
item.description: Moderate calorie restriction lowered an immune protein called C3 that appears to help drive chronic inflammation as the body ages. Blocking the same protein reduced age related inflammation in mice, raising the possibility that future treatments could mimic some benefits of calorie restriction without severe dieting. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Could the delay to China’s moon mission ease pressure on Nasa?
item.description: China’s delay of a high-stakes mission to hunt for water ice near the moon’s south pole may slow its lunar ambitions, but is unlikely to change the bigger contest with the United States over who can build a lasting presence on the moon, according to space experts. No reason was given when Chang’e-7 was postponed until next year, just hours before Sunday night’s scheduled lift-off, though a major tropical storm was approaching the launch site. Chinese space authorities said only that the mission... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: What has the return‑to‑office movement taught us? People, not technology, help companies get ahead
item.description: We like to believe that whatever ails a company can be fixed by digitizing it. And technology is easy to swap. Rip out the old system, bolt in the new one, declare yourself modern. But a company is not its buildings, its machines or its software. It is the people in it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 190-year-old DNA reveals a hidden pangolin species
item.description: DNA from a nearly 190-year-old museum specimen has helped scientists confirm a distinct Himalayan pangolin species hiding in plain sight in Nepal and northern India. The discovery could give conservationists a powerful new way to trace illegally traded pangolin scales back to the species and regions being targeted by poachers. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Human rights expert explains why labor trafficking often hides in plain sight
item.description: It can happen in fields, restaurants, hotels and construction sites—a type of human trafficking often hiding in plain sight and receiving far less media coverage. Labor trafficking is a human rights violation in which individuals are forced to perform labor or services through force, fraud or coercion. The National Human Trafficking Hotline identifies examples including domestic workers forced to work in homes, farmworkers coerced through violence as they harvest crops or factory workers held in inhumane conditions with little to no pay. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Manhattan-sized ice island breaks off Greenland’s Petermann Glacier
item.description: A Manhattan-sized ice island has broken away from Greenland’s Petermann Glacier after years of growing fractures weakened its floating ice tongue. Scientists expect two more huge sections could soon detach, potentially removing about 22 percent of the remaining ice tongue. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Do customer loyalty programs actually work? The benefits are in the eye of the cardholder
item.description: Whether you love a loyalty discount at the supermarket or frequently forget your loyalty card, loyalty programs (LPs) can be an essential support for families and households amid growing cost-of-living pressures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hyperdoped silicon photodiode advances short-wave infrared detection at room temperature
item.description: Detecting short-wave infrared (SWIR) light, a region of the electromagnetic spectrum just beyond the light visible to the human eye, could be advantageous for many real-world applications. For instance, it could enable more advanced systems for capturing images at night, as well as sophisticated medical imaging, environmental monitoring and industrial inspection technologies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Appropriated racial oppression shapes Black parents' socialization of children
item.description: Black parents who experienced higher levels of appropriated racial oppression—defined as shaping one's behavior and self-concept around dominant cultural norms of whiteness—were less likely to transmit positive, culturally protective messages that affirmed racial pride and self-worth to their adolescent children, a recent study found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: David Rosario ha comentado: National Geographic images like this remind us that behind every "perfect" shot is real risk and real people.
item.description: Photographer Cory Richards captured climbers near the summit of Gasherbrum II in Pakistan’s Karakoram Range in 2011. During the descent, the climbers,... Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Support groups for parents halved violence against children in wartime Ukraine, trial finds
item.description: Ukrainian parents who joined a support group program called "Hope Groups," designed for families living through the war, reported that violence against children was cut in half and that they had less than half the depression and anxiety symptoms of parents who had not yet participated in the program, according to a new trial led by the University of Oxford. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What you eat before age 2 may affect your health 70 years later
item.description: Britain’s postwar sugar rationing created a rare natural experiment that let researchers examine how early sugar exposure might affect health decades later. People who experienced more rationing during their first 1,000 days had lower rates of several cancers and showed signs of slower biological aging. They were also still eating less sugar and maintaining healthier diets around age 50. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Researchers map tick habitat to strengthen African swine fever preparedness
item.description: A small, nest-dwelling tick found across large parts of Texas could play an outsized role in how the United States responds to African swine fever (ASF) should the virus reach domestic or wild pigs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: French astronaut Adenot takes part in second spacewalk
item.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot began a second spacewalk at the International Space Station on Tuesday, as she and NASA astronaut Anil Menon were set to continue work on a space-to-ground communications antenna. Adenot, a European Space Agency astronaut, was scheduled to help Menon retrieve and install a spare antenna on the station’s Z1 truss, above the Unity module, and make electrical and data connections to restore high-speed communications with mission control. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Utah mountain ranges may store a billion tons of hidden ice
item.description: Unlike conventional glaciers, rock glaciers appear as piles of rock that obscure large masses of unaccounted-for ice. Rock glaciers are common in the Wasatch and Uinta ranges, even appearing on the Colorado Plateau in the La Sal Mountains near Moab. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New quantum computing method broadens spectroscopy of hard-to-model matter
item.description: Scientists could have a new way to explore the hidden behavior of matter, thanks to research involving Queen Mary University of London that uses a quantum computer to carry out a new form of computational spectroscopy. Fuente: Phys.org.
